reviews.title: I like this case
reviews.comment: I have this case with a Titan 360 aio and three extra fans for a total of nine fans. 9800x3d undervolted and running 5.4ghz. Rtx 5080 Clocked at 3225 Mhz. Idle cpu 42 gpu 31. Cyberpunk benchmark temps in second pic. Stays fairly quiet with cpu spikes in 70s. I have the rad in the back. I have 5 fans pulling in an 4 pushing air out. I also have the white rx120 version. LX fans are quieter.
reviews.author: Chris Wilson

reviews.title: Surprisingly great case
reviews.comment:
I was not sure how this case would compare to the 6500x or 2500x in terms of cabling space and routing or overall esthetics. Even once the case was in and I was planning everything out, I was skeptical.
Boy did it turn out better than I expect.  The cable management was a lot easier to route and take care of, build quality is in par with Corsair, everything fit the way you would want from a standard mid-size case. Of course, have the iCue Link fans makes cabling a lot easier as there is just 2 cables at most for fans to route into the back.
I have a mix of LX and RX fans, all 120mm, and the airflow is pretty steady. With a Titan 360mm AIO, I am seeing CPU and main board temps staying steady in the 30-40*C range, which is awesome. GPU still runs hot at around 70*C but I think that is more about the age (Sapphire 5700XT Nitro+) than with the case.
Absolutely love the included GPU anti-sag bracket, the function of the modular design, and how easy it is to access compared to previous cases (CM 690II Advanced and Corsair Graphite 780T).
Bottom line, for a budget case and build, huge improvement and esthetics all around.
